"Your life is not on the line. Mine is."

Six families had already buried someone, and he wanted the judge to feel sorry for him.

Darrell Brooks. Waukesha, Wisconsin, 2021. More than 60 people hurt, many of them kids marching in the parade.

And the $1,000 wasn't a typo. The county DA's office later admitted it was "inappropriately low." He was out for two days.

At trial he chose to represent himself. He told the court that wasn't his name. He got removed from the courtroom again and again. And when the judge pushed back, he got offended: "You think this is a whole game to me?"

Then a mother walked up to the podium.

Her daughter Olivia was 8, performing in the parade with her teammates. He hit the mother too. Then she spent five minutes walking between little girls curled up on the street, checking each one, looking for her own.

Olivia lived, after two weeks in the hospital with brain injuries.

All day in court she watched him roll his eyes at the families. So she said it to his face:

"You're a child killer. A woman killer. I cannot wait until somebody inflicts that harm on you."

In the video below, wait for the last 10 seconds. That's how he talked on the day he got sentenced.

He got six life sentences without parole, plus 762 years.

He ran a woman over, paid $1,000, and two days later six people were dead. Should the people who let him out answer for this parade too, or is every one of those deaths on him alone?

A social media influencer filmed himself and a friend allegedly raping a heavily intoxicated woman after offering her a lift home from a pub, a court has heard. 

Augustine Mitchell, 39, who posts online under the name LV/General and has hundreds of thousands of followers on platforms including YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, is standing trial at the Old Bailey alongside Marcel Johnson, also 39. 

Prosecutor Marion Smullen told jurors that Mitchell offered to take the 20-year-old woman home as she waited for an Uber after leaving a pub in Canary Wharf. Instead, the pair allegedly took her to their home, where she was raped and the acts were filmed. 

Ms Smullen said: “The prosecution case is that [the woman] was too drunk to give proper consent to have sexual intercourse with those men that particular night.” The court heard the complainant had consumed a large amount of alcohol that evening, including four strawberry daiquiris, two Bacardi and orange drinks, six tequila shots and a BuzzBall, as well as using nitrous oxide. Jurors were told the woman later told police that Mitchell had raped her from behind while Johnson forced her to perform a sexual act. 

Mitchell denies one count of rape. Johnson denies two counts. 

The trial is expected to last around two weeks and continues.

Via ( fxshionconcept )
